
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(gtools)
library(reshape2)
library(scales)
library(withr)
library(backports)
library(crayon)
library(vctrs)
library(pillar)
library(labeling)

library(ggplot2)
library(farver)


### Main function

heatmapVisualization <- function(main_matrix, quadratic_matrix, interactions_list, type, absoluteValue, scale, 
                                 include = rep(1, ncol(main_matrix)), fullRange = "TRUE", ranges, 
                                 pdfOut = FALSE, pdfName = NULL){
  
  ## Reduce data if only few parameters are of interest
  
  main_matrix <- main_matrix[, as.logical(include)]
  quadratic_matrix <- quadratic_matrix[, as.logical(include)]
  
  for(i in 1:length(interactions_list)){
    interactions_list[[i]] <- interactions_list[[i]][as.logical(include), as.logical(include)]
  }
  quadratic_matrix <- quadratic_matrix[, as.logical(include)]
  
  
  ## Sum effects appropriately
  
  if(type == "mainOnly"){
      outputData <- main_matrix
      titleVal = "Main effects only"
  }
  # Interpretation: potential of effect on Response if process parameter increased by one
  # independent on other parameters, so "ranges" of other parameters do not contribute here
  
  
  if(type == "mainQuadraticOnly"){
    outputData <- sign(main_matrix)*(abs(main_matrix) + abs(quadratic_matrix))
    titleVal = "Main and Quadratic effects only"
  }
  # Interpretation: potential of effect on Response if process parameter increased by one
  # regardless if increase is from -1 to 0 or from 0 to +1
  # independent on other parameters, so "ranges" of other parameters do not contribute here
  
  if(type == "allEffects"){
    
    allEffects <- sign(main_matrix)*(abs(main_matrix) + abs(quadratic_matrix))
    
    for(i in 1:nrow(main_matrix)){
      respData <- interactions_list[[i]]
      
      if(any(respData != 0)){
        effects <- which(respData !=0, arr.ind = T)
        
        for (j in 1:nrow(effects)){
          effectSize <- respData[effects[j, 1], effects[j,2]]
          
          if(fullRange == TRUE){
            allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]] <- sign(allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]])*(abs(allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]]) + abs(effectSize))
            allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]] <- sign(allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]])*(abs(allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]]) + abs(effectSize))
          } else {
            
            if(sign(allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]]) == 1){
              allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]] <- allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]] + max(effectSize*ranges[effects[j, 2],])
            } else {
              allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]] <- allEffects[i, effects[j, 1]] + min(effectSize*ranges[effects[j, 2],])
            }
            
            if(sign(allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]]) == 1){
              allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]] <- allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]] + max(effectSize*ranges[effects[j, 1],])
            } else {
              allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]] <- allEffects[i, effects[j, 2]] + min(effectSize*ranges[effects[j, 1],])
            }
          }
        }
        
      } 
      
    }
    
    outputData <-   allEffects
    titleVal = "Main, quadratic and interaction effects"
  }
  # Interpretation: potential of effect on Response if process parameter increased by one under certain setting of other parameters
  # depends on ranges of other parameters => need to take them into account
  
  
  if(scale == "original"){
    plotData <- melt(outputData)
  }
  
  # Scale the MPI per response
  if(scale == "perResponse"){
    outputDataResc <- outputData
    
    for (i in 1:nrow(outputDataResc)){
      maxEff <- max(abs(outputData[i,]))
      if(maxEff > 0) {outputDataResc[i,] <- outputData[i,]/maxEff}
    }
    plotData <- melt(outputDataResc)
  }

  # plotting part
  colnames(plotData) <- c("Var", "PP", "value")

  if(absoluteValue == TRUE) {
    
    p <- ggplot(plotData, aes(Var, PP)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = abs(value)), colour = "white") + 
      scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "black")
    base_size <- 9
    plotFinal <- p + theme_grey(base_size = base_size) + ylab("Process Factor") + xlab("Response") +  
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90, hjust=0)) + 
      scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      labs(title = paste0(titleVal, ": absolute value")) +
      theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
            plot.title = element_text(size = 14))
    
  } else {
    p <- ggplot(plotData, aes(Var, PP)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = value), colour = "white") + 
      scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("gold3","white","forestgreen"), values = rescale(c(min(plotData$value), 0, max(plotData$value))))
    base_size <- 9
    plotFinal <- p + theme_grey(base_size = base_size) + ylab("Process Factor") + xlab("Response") +  
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0)) + 
      scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      labs(title = titleVal) +
      theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
            plot.title = element_text(size = 14))
    
    
  }
  
  print(plotFinal)
  
  # output plot as pdf (used for manuscript)
  if (pdfOut == TRUE){
    pdf(file = pdfName)
    plot(plotFinal)
    dev.off()
  }
  
}


```

## The pastry dough experiment

### Data

Load the input data (coefficient estimates based on selected models). 

```{r loadData, echo = FALSE, eval = FALSE}

### NOTE: this chunk is not run, just shows preparation of the data that are saved i nRData file for readers convenience

dataPath <- "YOURPATH"

mainEffects <- read.csv(paste0(dataPath, "Data_Pastry_resultsGLS_main.csv"),header = TRUE, sep = ",", dec = ".")
rownames(mainEffects) <- mainEffects[, 1]
mainEffects <- mainEffects[, -1]
mainEffects <- as.matrix(mainEffects)

quadraticEffects <- read.csv(paste0(dataPath, "Data_Pastry_resultsGLS_quadr.csv"),header = TRUE, sep = ",", dec = ".")
rownames(quadraticEffects) <- quadraticEffects[, 1]
quadraticEffects <- quadraticEffects[, -1]
quadraticEffects <- as.matrix(quadraticEffects)

interactions <- vector("list", nrow(quadraticEffects)) 
names(interactions) <- rownames(quadraticEffects)

for (i in 1:nrow(quadraticEffects)){
  intTemp <- read.csv(paste0(dataPath, "Data_Pastry_resultsGLS_Int_y", i,".csv"), header = TRUE, sep = ",", dec = ".")
  rownames(intTemp) <- intTemp[, 1]
  intTemp <- intTemp[, -1]
  intTemp <- as.matrix(intTemp)
  interactions[[i]] <- intTemp
}

save(mainEffects, quadraticEffects, interactions, file = paste0(dataPath, "PastryDough_modelResults.RData"))

```


The main the quadratic and the interaction effects for the first response, as an example, are shown below. Note that $0.00$ means that the term has not been included in the final model.  

```{r dataExample, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
# Main effects
mainEffects
# Quadratic effects
quadraticEffects
# Interaction effects
interactions[[1]]
```
### Maximal possible influence on raw scale

Heatmap for the main effects only. 

```{r main, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "mainOnly",
                     absoluteValue = FALSE,
                     scale = "original")
```

We can add the quadratic effects. We show the maximal possible increase (MPI), either by moving from -1 to 0 or from 0 to +1. Conveniently, the MPI can be obtained by summing the absolute values of the main and the quadratic effects and by multiplying with the original sign of the main effect.     

```{r quadr, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "mainQuadraticOnly",
                     absoluteValue = FALSE,
                     scale = "original")
```

Analogously, we can add interaction effects. We display the maximal effect that the increase of a particular parameter can cause, when the other parameters are at values of -1 or +1, so the interaction effect sign coincides with the main effect sign. 

```{r inter, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "allEffects",
                     absoluteValue = FALSE,
                     scale = "original")
```


### Scaling 

```{r scaling, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "allEffects",
                     absoluteValue = FALSE,
                     scale = "perResponse")
```

### Absolute value

```{r absscale, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "allEffects",
                     absoluteValue = TRUE,
                     scale = "perResponse",
                     #pdfOut = TRUE, 
                     #pdfName = "perResponseScaleAbs_PD.pdf"
                     )
```


### Considerations for follow-up experiment


#### Remove process parameters


```{r subset, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "allEffects",
                     absoluteValue = TRUE,
                     scale = "perResponse",
                     include = c(1,1,0),
                     #pdfOut = TRUE, 
                     #pdfName = "perResponseScaleAbs_remove_PD.pdf"
                     )
```

#### Change the range of the factors


```{r ranges, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
restrictedRanges = matrix(rep(c(-1,1), each = ncol(mainEffects)), ncol = 2, byrow = FALSE)
restrictedRanges[3, ] <- c(-0.1, 0.1)
colnames(restrictedRanges) <- c("lower", "upper")
rownames(restrictedRanges) <- colnames(mainEffects)
restrictedRanges

heatmapVisualization(main_matrix = mainEffects, 
                     quadratic_matrix = quadraticEffects,
                     interactions_list = interactions,
                     type = "allEffects",
                     absoluteValue = TRUE,
                     scale = "perResponse",
                     fullRange = FALSE,
                     ranges = restrictedRanges,
                     #pdfOut = TRUE, 
                     #pdfName = "perResponseScaleAbs_restrict_PD.pdf"
                     )


```

## The simulated data

### Data

Simulate the modelling result of the hypothetical data. 

```{r simulate2, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE}


# number of factors
nPars <- 11
# number of responses
nResp <- 20
# probability of presence of quadratic effect
probQuadratic <- 0.2
# probability of presence of interaction effect
probInteraction <- 0.30


mainEffects <- quadraticEffects <- matrix(numeric(nPars*nResp), nrow = nResp)
colnames(mainEffects) <- colnames(quadraticEffects) <- paste0("Factor_", 1:nPars)
rownames(mainEffects) <- rownames(quadraticEffects) <- paste0("Response_", 1:nResp)

interactions <- vector("list", nResp) 
names(interactions) <- paste0("Response_", 1:nResp)

for (i in 1:nResp){
  interactions[[i]] <- matrix(numeric(nPars*nPars), nrow = nPars)
  colnames(interactions[[i]]) <-   rownames(interactions[[i]]) <-   colnames(mainEffects)
}


set.seed(1234)

for(i in 1:nResp){
  # select randomly how many factors are selected
  numberSelected <- sample(2:(nPars-1), 1, replace = TRUE)
  # select randomly which ones are selected
  mainEffectsSelected <- sort(sample(1:nPars, numberSelected, replace = FALSE))
  
  for(j in 1:length(mainEffectsSelected)){
    # generate main effect size
    mainEffects[i, mainEffectsSelected[j]] <- round(rnorm(1, 0, 5), 2)
    
    # generate quadratic effect size, with probability of 0.2 of presence of quadratic effect
    if(rbinom(1, 1, probQuadratic) == 1){
      quadraticEffects[i, mainEffectsSelected[j]] <- round(rnorm(1, 0, 5), 2)
    }
    
  }
  
  # generate interaction effects
  perm <- permutations(n = numberSelected, r = 2, v = mainEffectsSelected)
  
  if(nrow(perm) > 2){
    comb <- perm[perm[, 1] <= perm[, 2], ]
    intID <- as.logical(rbinom(nrow(comb), 1, probInteraction))
    
    if (sum(intID) == 1){
      interactions[[i]][comb[intID, 1], comb[intID, 2]] <- round(rnorm(1, 0, 5), 2)
    }
    
    if(sum(intID) > 1){
      comb <- comb[intID, ]
      for (j in 1:nrow(comb)){
        
        interactions[[i]][comb[j, 1], comb[j, 2]] <- round(rnorm(1, 0, 5), 2)
        
      }
    }
  } else {

    if(rbinom(1, 1, probInteraction)){
      interactions[[i]][perm[1, 1], perm[1, 2]] <- round(rnorm(1, 0, 5), 2)
    }
  }
  
}


## Inflate main/quadratic effects for certain factors (2, 6, 11) to get better contrast of results
mainEffects[, 2] <- mainEffects[,2]*5
mainEffects[, 6] <- mainEffects[,6]*5
mainEffects[, 11] <- mainEffects[,11]*5

quadraticEffects[, 2] <- quadraticEffects[,2]*5
quadraticEffects[, 6] <- quadraticEffects[,6]*5
quadraticEffects[, 11] <- quadraticEffects[,11]*5



```
